samples.summary: New `!readOnly &&` guard on `canUndo`/`canRedo` is covered only by an assertion that passes regardless
samples.evidence: `initialize` now returns `canUndo: () => !readOnly && store.canUndo()` (packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:672-674). The only coverage is `expect(api.canUndo()).toBe(false)` / `canRedo()` in the new 'lets no write reach the store on a read-only mount' test — but in that test no write ever lands, so the underlying `MemNoteStore.canUndo()` is already `false` and the assertion holds with or without the new guard. No test constructs a read-only mount over a store that actually has history (e.g. a store pre-edited before `initialize`, or a spy returning `true`), so the guard is untested. Impact is contained: a regression only re-enables a toolbar button whose action is a no-op.

samples.summary: Divider resize change (`track = rect.width - divider.offsetWidth`, 25px hit area, `touch-action: none`) has no test
samples.evidence: The diff changes the split-pane drag math from `ratio = (x - left) / rect.width` to `/ track` and enlarges the divider to 25px with `touchAction = 'none'`. Grepping packages/notes/src for `divider|splitRatio|pointerdown|touchAction` finds matches only in editor.ts — editor.test.ts has no divider/drag test at all. A wrong `track` (e.g. `offsetWidth` reported as 0 or the subtraction inverted) silently mis-tracks the pointer during pane resize, a user-visible interaction, with nothing to catch it. A test could dispatch pointerdown/pointermove with a stubbed `getBoundingClientRect`/`offsetWidth` and assert the resulting flex basis.

samples.summary: The new `EditorState.readOnly` / remote-only `changeFilter` gates are masked by the store wrapper, so no test can fail if they are removed
samples.evidence: `initialize` now applies three independent gates on a read-only mount: the `readOnlyNoteStore` wrap (editor.ts:249), `EditorState.readOnly.of(readOnly)` and the remote-only `changeFilter`. The new test 'lets no write reach the store on a read-only mount' asserts only that `store.editText` was never called and the text is unchanged — which the store wrapper alone guarantees, since every transaction ends at the neutered `editText`. Deleting the `changeFilter` (or `EditorState.readOnly`) would leave the whole suite green. Also, the paths the comment names (paste, drop, image upload, preview checkbox) are not exercised; only four toolbar commands plus undo/redo are. Consider asserting the filter directly (e.g. that a local `view.dispatch` leaves `view.state.doc` unchanged) so each layer is independently pinned.

samples.summary: The layout's "no localStorage writes" claim is tested only for viewMode, not keymap or showAuthors
samples.evidence: `SharedNotesLayout`'s docstring says the state is the workspace route's 'minus every localStorage write', and it wires `onKeymapChange={setKeymap}` / `onShowAuthorsChange={setShowAuthors}` (shared-notes-layout.tsx:109-111). Only the view-mode case is pinned ('applies a view-mode change without persisting it', asserting `wafflebase:notes:viewMode` still reads 'both'). No test toggles the keymap or the blame gutter and asserts `wafflebase:notes:keymap` / `wafflebase:notes:showAuthors` are untouched, so a future swap to `writeKeymap`/`writeShowAuthors` (as `notes-detail` does) would overwrite an anonymous visitor's per-browser preference undetected.

samples.summary: `NotesView`'s own `readOnly ? readOnlyNoteStore(raw) : raw` wrapping has no frontend test
samples.evidence: The diff adds a store wrap inside `NotesView` (notes-view.tsx:151-153). There is no `notes-view.test.tsx` (glob of packages/frontend/src/app/notes/*test* returns only notes-undo-integration, notes-toolbar, yorkie-note-store, notes-thumbnail), and the new shared-notes-layout test mocks `@/app/notes/notes-view` away entirely, so nothing exercises this branch. Impact is contained because `initialize()` also wraps and the wrapper is idempotent (covered in packages/notes/src/store/read-only.test.ts), but a regression here — e.g. handing the raw store to the thumbnail/registration path — would go unnoticed.

samples.summary: `expect(said).not.toContain('token=')` is true regardless of the code under test
samples.evidence: The shadow log line is a fixed template `[shadow] would deny method=… target=… status=… reason=…` (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:160-162) and no code path anywhere emits `token=`; the construction warning does not either. The assertion therefore passes whether or not the token is ever logged, and would keep passing if the token were logged under a different label (e.g. `tok=` or interpolated bare). A stronger form would assert the emitted line does not contain the actual token value passed in (`'t'` is too short to match usefully — use a distinctive token string).

samples.summary: `shareTokenImageUploader` is mocked with a different shape than the real function, so the uploader wiring test proves little beyond "a function was passed"
samples.evidence: The test mocks `@/app/docs/image-insert` with `shareTokenImageUploader: (token) => async () => `uploaded:${token}``, then asserts `uploadImage()` resolves to 'uploaded:tok-1'. The real uploader takes a `File` argument; the mock ignores arity, so a mis-wired call signature (or passing the wrong argument through to `NotesView`) would not be caught. It does correctly pin that the token reaches the factory and that a viewer gets `undefined`, which is the main point — hence nit.

samples.summary: `subscribePresence` (an allowlisted reader) and the allowlist's default-deny property are not exercised
samples.evidence: `NOTE_STORE_READERS` includes `subscribePresence`, but read-only.test.ts only exercises `getText`, `getAuthorSpans`, `getPeerSelections`, `canUndo` and `subscribeRemote`. If `subscribePresence` were dropped from the allowlist the wrapper would return `undefined` and a viewer mount would lose peer presence, with no test failing. Likewise nothing asserts the stated default-deny property (an unlisted member is neutered rather than forwarded), which is the wrapper's central design claim.
